## Classes

### <a name="soundwave"></a>`soundwave`

Soundwave pushes one merged set of findings into Puppet Enterprise's
Vulnerability Remediation service. It never parses a scanner. Each cassette
writes the scanner-neutral findings file (docs/findings-file.md) into
$cassette_dir and Soundwave merges whatever is there, so a third scanner is
another cassette rather than another integration.

Two cassettes ship with it, each named for its scanner, and two more,
**nessus** and **rapid7**, are experimental and off by default. The **openvas**
cassette reads Greenbone over GMP, and is on by default. The **vuls** cassette
reads the run the vuls module last recorded as complete, and is off by
default. Each runs before the push, and one that fails leaves its previous
file in place, so the push still goes and the cassette's staleness alert says
how old that file is. Neither is given a platform to own: they may report the
same host, package and CVE, and sorting out what overlaps is Soundwave's job
rather than a convention either of them keeps.

This was openvas_transformer until 2026-09-16. It keeps the same transformer
ID, fqdn_uuid of the node's certname, so VR's history carries on unbroken.

#### Examples

##### Basic usage via Hiera

```puppet
include soundwave
```

##### <a name="-soundwave--pe_token"></a>`pe_token`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

PE authentication token with permission to push to the VRS service. Set
this or token_password, not both. A token given here sits in the catalogue
until someone replaces it by hand; token_password avoids both.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_password"></a>`token_password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[Sensitive[String[1]], Deferred]]`

Password of the PE user soundwave::rbac_user makes on the primary. Set, this
node mints its own token with rbac_token, renews it after
token_renew_after, and keeps it in token_file, which Soundwave reads at the
start of every run. Pass a Deferred such as node_encrypt::secret's: a
Sensitive class parameter is recorded in the catalogue in plaintext. Needs
conductor-rbac in the Puppetfile.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_login"></a>`token_login`

Data type: `String[1]`

That user's login.

Default value: `'soundwave'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_file"></a>`token_file`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Where the token is kept, root only.

Default value: `'/opt/puppetlabs/soundwave/python/pe.token'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_lifetime"></a>`token_lifetime`

Data type: `String[1]`

Lifetime of each token minted, in PE's units (`30d`, `12h`).

Default value: `'30d'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_renew_after"></a>`token_renew_after`

Data type: `String[1]`

Age after which the token is replaced on the next Puppet run. Shorter than
token_lifetime, by more than the agent's run interval.

Default value: `'21d'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_server"></a>`token_server`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Host]`

Console host to mint the token from. Defaults to pe_host, the primary.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--token_port"></a>`token_port`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Port]`

Console port. Defaults to rbac_token's own, 4433.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--pe_host"></a>`pe_host`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Host]`

PE primary to push to. Defaults to the Puppet server that compiled this
catalogue, so it only needs setting when that isn't the PE primary, or when
there is no server at all (`puppet apply`).

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--threat_intel"></a>`threat_intel`

Data type: `Enum['off', 'download', 'directory']`

Mark every check with exploit data from CISA's Known Exploited
Vulnerabilities catalogue and FIRST's EPSS scores, joined on CVE, so every
scanner gets the same answer whether or not it reports either. `download`
fetches both files into threat_intel_dir on each run, and a failed download
keeps the previous file. `directory` reads whatever is copied into
threat_intel_dir, for a node with no internet access: CISA's
`known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json` and FIRST's
`epss_scores-current.csv.gz`, or that file unpacked as `.csv`. `off`, the
default, leaves checks as the scanners wrote them.

Default value: `'off'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--threat_intel_dir"></a>`threat_intel_dir`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Where the two feed files live.

Default value: `'/var/lib/soundwave/threat-intel'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--threat_intel_in_vr"></a>`threat_intel_in_vr`

Data type: `Boolean`

Lead each finding's summary in PE with what threat_intel found, for example
`Known exploited (CISA KEV). EPSS 0.91, 99.8th percentile.` PE's schema has
no field for either, so the summary is the only place it can show. It
changes text the console already displays, so it's off by default, and it
does nothing while threat_intel is `off` unless a scanner reports KEV itself.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-soundwave--kev_url"></a>`kev_url`

Data type: `Stdlib::HTTPUrl`

Where `download` fetches the KEV catalogue from. Point it at an internal
mirror if there is one.

Default value: `'https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--epss_url"></a>`epss_url`

Data type: `Stdlib::HTTPUrl`

Where `download` fetches the EPSS scores from.

Default value: `'https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--findings_api_host"></a>`findings_api_host`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Host]`

Host running a findings API, for the author's own consumer, whose API isn't
published. Unset disables the push, which is the default. Set, Soundwave
sends each cassette there unmerged as well as pushing to VR, including
while the transformer is still pending in PE. It authenticates with this
node's Puppet agent certificate.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--findings_api_port"></a>`findings_api_port`

Data type: `Stdlib::Port`

Port for that API.

Default value: `10051`

##### <a name="-soundwave--correlate"></a>`correlate`

Data type: `Boolean`

Report what correlation would join, without joining anything. Findings from
every cassette are grouped by certname, CVE, subject and fix type, and the
counts plus a bounded sample go to the log and the metrics file. Nothing
downstream changes: VR still gets a row per finding and a findings API
still gets each cassette verbatim. Off by default, because the count is worth having
before the merge is.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-soundwave--compose_findings"></a>`compose_findings`

Data type: `Boolean`

Act on correlation rather than only report it. Findings that
share a correlation group are composed into one record: VR gets one row per
weakness across both cassettes, carrying every check's CVEs, the highest
per-CVE score, and a sentence naming the checks it came from. A findings API
stays one cassette per push and gets sets composed within a cassette only, with
each member's own values in `contributors`. A set over 5 findings or 10 CVEs
is left alone and counted, so one wide advisory cannot chain unrelated
findings together. Off by default: it changes what the VR console shows.
The correlation_exceptions below apply here too.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-soundwave--correlation_exceptions"></a>`correlation_exceptions`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Check-ID pairs that must never be correlated, as `a|b,c|d`. For pairs the
key provably cannot separate: the SSH protocol check and the OpenSSH
version check both report CVE-2023-48795 on port 22 with the same fix type,
and one is closed by upgrading a package while the other is closed by
disabling algorithms. Seeded from what the sample turns up.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--min_confidence"></a>`min_confidence`

Data type: `Integer[0, 100]`

QoD floor applied when mapping the merged findings to VR. Cassettes record
every finding with its confidence; VR has nowhere to put one, so a
low-confidence finding there reads the same as a certain one. 70 is gvmd's
own default and keeps PE showing exactly what it showed before.

Default value: `70`

##### <a name="-soundwave--host_map_file"></a>`host_map_file`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

JSON object mapping each scanned address to its Puppet certname. Hosts found
in it are sent to PE under their certname; anything else keeps the name gvmd
had and is recorded in the cassette's unmapped list. With the openvas
cassette on it defaults to the openvas module's `scan-hosts.json`, beside
`compose_file`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--metrics_file"></a>`metrics_file`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

If set, each run writes a node_exporter textfile here: when it ran, whether
it worked, PE's HTTP status, whether VR has accepted the transformer, and
per cassette its age, findings, host states and what its filters dropped.
It's written while the transformer is still pending too. Point it into the
textfile collector's directory.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--post_body_filepath"></a>`post_body_filepath`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

If set, the JSON body of the PE request is written here for debugging.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-soundwave--transformer_name"></a>`transformer_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Display name registered with PE.

Default value: `'Soundwave'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--transformer_description"></a>`transformer_description`

Data type: `String[1]`

Description registered with PE.

Default value: `'Soundwave: merged scanner findings'`

### <a name="soundwave--rbac_user"></a>`soundwave::rbac_user`

Declare this on the PE primary, where the RBAC types can reach the console
with the primary's own certificate. It makes a role that can register a
transformer and push to Vulnerability Remediation and nothing else, and a
user holding only that role. Give soundwave's own node the same password as
`soundwave::token_password` and it mints and renews its own short-lived
token, so no token is ever in a catalogue.

The RBAC types come from conductor-rbac (albatrossflavour's fork, whose
rbac_token renews), which is not a metadata dependency: add it to the
Puppetfile as `rbac` before declaring this class.

#### Examples

##### On the primary, with the password from node_encrypt

```puppet
class { 'soundwave::rbac_user':
  password => node_encrypt::secret(lookup('soundwave::rbac_password')),
}
```

##### <a name="-soundwave--rbac_user--password"></a>`password`

Data type: `Variant[Sensitive[String[1]], Deferred]`

The user's password. A Sensitive class parameter is still written into the
catalogue in plaintext, since class parameters are recorded there, so pass
the Deferred that `node_encrypt::secret()` returns and the catalogue carries
only ciphertext the primary can open.

##### <a name="-soundwave--rbac_user--login"></a>`login`

Data type: `String[1]`

The user's login.

Default value: `'soundwave'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--rbac_user--role"></a>`role`

Data type: `String[1]`

The role's display name.

Default value: `'Soundwave'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--rbac_user--email"></a>`email`

Data type: `String[1]`

The user's email. The RBAC API insists on one.

Default value: `"soundwave@${facts['networking']['domain']}"`

##### <a name="-soundwave--rbac_user--display_name"></a>`display_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

The user's display name.

Default value: `'Soundwave'`

##### <a name="-soundwave--rbac_user--check_password"></a>`check_password`

Data type: `Boolean`

Log in as the user each run and reset the password if it has drifted.

Default value: `true`

## Tasks

### <a name="run_soundwave"></a>`run_soundwave`

Collect the Greenbone cassette and push the merged findings to PE

**Supports noop?** false
